title: अष्टपञ्चाशत्तमोऽध्यायः
titleEn: Adhyaya 58 · Fourth day: Bhima among the elephants

summary.en: Dhritarashtra laments that fate seems to favour the Pandavas. Duryodhana sends the Magadha elephant division against Bhima, who destroys them with his club like a god of death in a burning-ground.
summary.kn: ದೈವವು ಪಾಂಡವರ ಪರವಾಗಿದೆಯೆಂದು ಧೃತರಾಷ್ಟ್ರ ಪರಿತಪಿಸುತ್ತಾನೆ. ದುರ್ಯೋಧನ ಮಾಗಧನ ಆನೆದಳವನ್ನು ಭೀಮನ ಮೇಲೆ ಕಳುಹಿಸುತ್ತಾನೆ; ಭೀಮ ಗದೆಯಿಂದ ಅವನ್ನು ಸ್ಮಶಾನದಲ್ಲಿರುವ ರುದ್ರನಂತೆ ನಾಶಮಾಡುತ್ತಾನೆ.
summary.hi: धृतराष्ट्र विलाप करते हैं कि दैव पाण्डवों के पक्ष में लगता है। दुर्योधन मगध के हाथियों की सेना भीम पर भेजता है, और भीम श्मशान में रुद्र की तरह गदा से उसे नष्ट कर देते हैं।
summary.te: దైవం పాండవుల పక్షంగా ఉందని ధృతరాష్ట్రుడు విలపిస్తాడు. దుర్యోధనుడు మాగధుని ఏనుగుల దళాన్ని భీముని పైకి పంపుతాడు; భీముడు శ్మశానంలో రుద్రునిలా గదతో వాటిని నాశనం చేస్తాడు.
summary.ta: விதி பாண்டவர் பக்கம் இருப்பதாகத் த்ருதராஷ்டிரன் புலம்புகிறான். துரியோதனன் மகதனின் யானைப்படையைப் பீமன் மீது ஏவ, பீமன் சுடுகாட்டில் உருத்திரன் போல் கதையால் அதை அழிக்கிறான்.
summary.ml: വിധി പാണ്ഡവരെയാണ് അനുകൂലിക്കുന്നതെന്ന് ധൃതരാഷ്ട്രർ വിലപിക്കുന്നു. മഗധ ആനപ്പടയെ ദുര്യോധനൻ ഭീമനെതിരെ അയയ്ക്കുന്നു; ശ്മശാനത്തിലെ മൃത്യുദേവനെപ്പോലെ ഭീമൻ ഗദകൊണ്ട് അവരെ നശിപ്പിക്കുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 6.58; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Mon Jul 26 2021

verses.text: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच

meaning.en: Dhritarashtra said:

verses.text:
दैवमेव परं मन्ये पौरुषादपि संजय ।
यत्सैन्यं मम पुत्रस्य पाण्डुसैन्येन वध्यते ॥

meaning.en: I think fate is greater than human effort, Sanjaya, when my son's army is being cut down by the army of Pandu's sons.

verses.text:
नित्यं हि मामकांस्तात हतानेव हि शंससि ।
अव्यग्रांश्च प्रहृष्टांश्च नित्यं शंससि पाण्डवान् ॥

meaning.en: Always, my dear, you tell me only that my men are slain, and always you tell of the Pandavas as undismayed and joyful.

verses.text:
हीनान्पुरुषकारेण मामकानद्य संजय ।
पतितान्पात्यमानांश्च हतानेव च शंससि ॥

meaning.en: Today again, Sanjaya, you tell me that my men, lacking manly exertion, have fallen, are being felled, or are simply dead.

verses.text:
युध्यमानान्यथाशक्ति घटमानाञ्जयं प्रति ।
पाण्डवा विजयन्त्येव जीयन्ते चैव मामकाः ॥

meaning.en: Though fighting with all their strength and striving for victory, the Pandavas keep winning and my men keep losing.

verses.text:
सोऽहं तीव्राणि दुःखानि दुर्योधनकृतानि च ।
अश्रौषं सततं तात दुःसहानि बहूनि च ॥

meaning.en: So I have heard, my dear, unceasingly, many sharp and unbearable sorrows brought about by Duryodhana.

verses.text:
तमुपायं न पश्यामि जीयेरन्येन पाण्डवाः ।
मामका वा जयं युद्धे प्राप्नुयुर्येन संजय ॥

meaning.en: I do not see the means by which the Pandavas could be defeated, or by which my men could win the battle, Sanjaya.

verses.text: संजय उवाच

meaning.en: Sanjaya said:

verses.text:
क्षयं मनुष्यदेहानां गजवाजिरथक्षयम् ।
शृणु राजन्स्थिरो भूत्वा तवैवापनयो महान् ॥

meaning.en: Hear, king, with a steady mind, of the destruction of human bodies, elephants, horses and chariots; the great misfortune is of your own making.

verses.text:
धृष्टद्युम्नस्तु शल्येन पीडितो नवभिः शरैः ।
पीडयामास संक्रुद्धो मद्राधिपतिमायसैः ॥

meaning.en: Dhrishtadyumna, struck by Shalya with nine arrows, grew enraged and struck the lord of the Madras with iron arrows.

verses.text:
तत्राद्भुतमपश्याम पार्षतस्य पराक्रमम् ।
न्यवारयत यत्तूर्णं शल्यं समितिशोभनम् ॥

meaning.en: There we saw the marvelous prowess of Prishata's son, in how swiftly he held off Shalya, the ornament of assemblies.

verses.text:
नान्तरं ददृशे कश्चित्तयोः संरब्धयो रणे ।
मुहूर्तमिव तद्युद्धं तयोः सममिवाभवत् ॥

meaning.en: No one saw any gap between those two, enraged in the battle; for a moment the fight between them seemed even.

verses.text:
ततः शल्यो महाराज धृष्टद्युम्नस्य संयुगे ।
धनुश्चिच्छेद भल्लेन पीतेन निशितेन च ॥

meaning.en: Then Shalya, great king, cut Dhrishtadyumna's bow in the battle with a sharp yellow broad-headed arrow.

verses.text:
अथैनं शरवर्षेण छादयामास भारत ।
गिरिं जलागमे यद्वज्जलदा जलधारिणः ॥

meaning.en: Then, Bharata, he covered him with a rain of arrows, as rain-clouds cover a mountain in the rainy season.

verses.text:
अभिमन्युस्तु संक्रुद्धो धृष्टद्युम्ने निपीडिते ।
अभिदुद्राव वेगेन मद्रराजरथं प्रति ॥

meaning.en: But Abhimanyu, enraged to see Dhrishtadyumna hard pressed, rushed swiftly at the chariot of the king of the Madras.

verses.text:
ततो मद्राधिपरथं कार्ष्णिः प्राप्यातिकोपनः ।
आर्तायनिममेयात्मा विव्याध विशिखैस्त्रिभिः ॥

meaning.en: Then Krishna's grandson, immeasurable in spirit and very angry, reached the chariot of the lord of the Madras and pierced Shalya, Artayani, with three arrows.

verses.text:
ततस्तु तावका राजन्परीप्सन्तोऽऽर्जुनिं रणे ।
मद्रराजरथं तूर्णं परिवार्यावतस्थिरे ॥

meaning.en: Then your men, king, wishing to save Arjuna's son in the battle, quickly surrounded and stood around the chariot of the king of Madra.

verses.text:
दुर्योधनो विकर्णश्च दुःशासनविविंशती ।
दुर्मर्षणो दुःसहश्च चित्रसेनश्च दुर्मुखः ॥

meaning.en: Duryodhana, Vikarna, Duhshasana and Vivimshati, Durmarshana, Duhsaha, Chitrasena and Durmukha,

verses.text:
सत्यव्रतश्च भद्रं ते पुरुमित्रश्च भारत ।
एते मद्राधिपरथं पालयन्तः स्थिता रणे ॥

meaning.en: Satyavrata, and may good come to you, Bharata, Purumitra: these stood in the battle guarding the chariot of the lord of the Madras.

verses.text:
तान्भीमसेनः संक्रुद्धो धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पार्षतः ।
द्रौपदेयाभिमन्युश्च माद्रीपुत्रौ च पाण्डवौ ॥

meaning.en: Bhimasena enraged, Dhrishtadyumna son of Prishata, Draupadi's sons, Abhimanyu, and the two Pandavas, Madri's sons,

verses.text:
नानारूपाणि शस्त्राणि विसृजन्तो विशां पते ।
अभ्यवर्तन्त संहृष्टाः परस्परवधैषिणः ।
ते वै समीयुः संग्रामे राजन्दुर्मन्त्रिते तव ॥

meaning.en: hurling weapons of many kinds, lord of the people, attacked them, delighted and eager to kill one another. They met in that battle, king, because of your ill counsel.

verses.text:
तस्मिन्दाशरथे युद्धे वर्तमाने भयावहे ।
तावकानां परेषां च प्रेक्षका रथिनोऽभवन् ॥

meaning.en: While that fearsome battle, like the battle of Rama, Dasharatha's son, was going on, the chariot-warriors of both your side and theirs became spectators.

verses.text:
शस्त्राण्यनेकरूपाणि विसृजन्तो महारथाः ।
अन्योन्यमभिनर्दन्तः संप्रहारं प्रचक्रिरे ॥

meaning.en: The great chariot-warriors, hurling weapons of many kinds and roaring at each other, fought a close fight.

verses.text:
ते यत्ता जातसंरम्भाः सर्वेऽन्योन्यं जिघांसवः ।
महास्त्राणि विमुञ्चन्तः समापेतुरमर्षणाः ॥

meaning.en: All of them, intent, filled with fury and eager to kill one another, hurled great weapons and clashed, impatient with anger.

verses.text:
दुर्योधनस्तु संक्रुद्धो धृष्टद्युम्नं महारणे ।
विव्याध निशितैर्बाणैश्चतुर्भिस्त्वरितो भृशम् ॥

meaning.en: Duryodhana, enraged, quickly and sharply pierced Dhrishtadyumna in the great battle with four sharp arrows.

verses.text:
दुर्मर्षणश्च विंशत्या चित्रसेनश्च पञ्चभिः ।
दुर्मुखो नवभिर्बाणैर्दुःसहश्चापि सप्तभिः ।
विविंशतिः पञ्चभिश्च त्रिभिर्दुःशासनस्तथा ॥

meaning.en: Durmarshana struck him with twenty, Chitrasena with five, Durmukha with nine arrows, Duhsaha with seven, Vivimshati with five, and Duhshasana with three.

verses.text:
तान्प्रत्यविध्यद्राजेन्द्र पार्षतः शत्रुतापनः ।
एकैकं पञ्चविंशत्या दर्शयन्पाणिलाघवम् ॥

meaning.en: Prishata's son, scorcher of foes, king of kings, struck each of them back with twenty-five, showing the lightness of his hand.

verses.text:
सत्यव्रतं तु समरे पुरुमित्रं च भारत ।
अभिमन्युरविध्यत्तौ दशभिर्दशभिः शरैः ॥

meaning.en: Abhimanyu in the battle pierced Satyavrata and Purumitra, Bharata, each with ten arrows.

verses.text:
माद्रीपुत्रौ तु समरे मातुलं मातृनन्दनौ ।
छादयेतां शरव्रातैस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत् ॥

meaning.en: Madri's two sons, joy of their mother, covered their maternal uncle in the battle with swarms of arrows, and it was a wonder.

verses.text:
ततः शल्यो महाराज स्वस्रीयौ रथिनां वरौ ।
शरैर्बहुभिरानर्छत्कृतप्रतिकृतैषिणौ ।
छाद्यमानौ ततस्तौ तु माद्रीपुत्रौ न चेलतुः ॥

meaning.en: Then Shalya, great king, struck those two best of chariot-warriors, his sister's sons, with many arrows, though they sought to return like for like; yet, covered, Madri's two sons did not waver.

verses.text:
अथ दुर्योधनं दृष्ट्वा भीमसेनो महाबलः ।
विधित्सुः कलहस्यान्तं गदां जग्राह पाण्डवः ॥

meaning.en: Then, seeing Duryodhana, the mighty Bhima, the Pandava, wishing to end the quarrel, took up his mace.

verses.text:
तमुद्यतगदं दृष्ट्वा कैलासमिव शृङ्गिणम् ।
भीमसेनं महाबाहुं पुत्रास्ते प्राद्रवन्भयात् ॥

meaning.en: Seeing mighty-armed Bhimasena with raised mace, like Kailasa with its peaks, your sons fled in terror.

verses.text:
दुर्योधनस्तु संक्रुद्धो मागधं समचोदयत् ।
अनीकं दशसाहस्रं कुञ्जराणां तरस्विनाम् ।
मागधं पुरतः कृत्वा भीमसेनं समभ्ययात् ॥

meaning.en: Duryodhana, enraged, urged on the king of Magadha with an army of ten thousand swift elephants. Putting the Magadhan in front, he advanced on Bhimasena.

verses.text:
आपतन्तं च तं दृष्ट्वा गजानीकं वृकोदरः ।
गदापाणिरवारोहद्रथात्सिंह इवोन्नदन् ॥

meaning.en: Seeing that elephant army coming, Vrikodara, mace in hand, got down from his chariot, roaring like a lion.

verses.text:
अद्रिसारमयीं गुर्वीं प्रगृह्य महतीं गदाम् ।
अभ्यधावद्गजानीकं व्यादितास्य इवान्तकः ॥

meaning.en: Gripping his huge, heavy mace made of the essence of mountains, he ran at the elephants like Death with open mouth.

verses.text:
स गजान्गदया निघ्नन्व्यचरत्समरे बली ।
भीमसेनो महाबाहुः सवज्र इव वासवः ॥

meaning.en: The strong, mighty-armed Bhimasena moved about in battle, striking elephants with his mace, like Vasava with his thunderbolt.

verses.text:
तस्य नादेन महता मनोहृदयकम्पिना ।
व्यत्यचेष्टन्त संहत्य गजा भीमस्य नर्दतः ॥

meaning.en: At his great roar that shook minds and hearts, the elephants of the roaring Bhima huddled and flailed about.

verses.text:
ततस्तु द्रौपदीपुत्राः सौभद्रश्च महारथः ।
नकुलः सहदेवश्च धृष्टद्युम्नश्च पार्षतः ॥

meaning.en: Then Draupadi's sons, the great chariot-warrior Abhimanyu, Nakula and Sahadeva, and Dhrishtadyumna son of Prishata,

verses.text:
पृष्ठं भीमस्य रक्षन्तः शरवर्षेण वारणान् ।
अभ्यधावन्त वर्षन्तो मेघा इव गिरीन्यथा ॥

meaning.en: guarding Bhima's back, rushed at the elephants raining arrows, like clouds raining on mountains.

verses.text:
क्षुरैः क्षुरप्रैर्भल्लैश्च पीतैरञ्जलिकैरपि ।
पातयन्तोत्तमाङ्गानि पाण्डवा गजयोधिनाम् ॥

meaning.en: With razors, kshurapras, broad-headed shafts, yellow arrows and anjalikas, the Pandavas brought down the heads of the elephant-fighters.

verses.text:
शिरोभिः प्रपतद्भिश्च बाहुभिश्च विभूषितैः ।
अश्मवृष्टिरिवाभाति पाणिभिश्च सहाङ्कुशैः ॥

meaning.en: With heads falling and ornamented arms, and hands with goads, it looked like a rain of stones.

verses.text:
हृतोत्तमाङ्गाः स्कन्धेषु गजानां गजयोधिनः ।
अदृश्यन्ताचलाग्रेषु द्रुमा भग्नशिखा इव ॥

meaning.en: The elephant-riders, their heads cut off, were seen on the elephants' shoulders like trees with broken tops on mountain peaks.

verses.text:
धृष्टद्युम्नहतानन्यानपश्याम महागजान् ।
पतितान्पात्यमानांश्च पार्षतेन महात्मना ॥

meaning.en: We saw other great elephants killed by Dhrishtadyumna, fallen or being felled by great-souled Prishata's son.

verses.text:
मागधोऽथ महीपालो गजमैरावतोपमम् ।
प्रेषयामास समरे सौभद्रस्य रथं प्रति ॥

meaning.en: Then the king of Magadha sent an elephant like Airavata at the chariot of Subhadra's son in the battle.

verses.text:
तमापतन्तं संप्रेक्ष्य मागधस्य गजोत्तमम् ।
जघानैकेषुणा वीरः सौभद्रः परवीरहा ॥

meaning.en: Seeing that best of Magadha's elephants coming, the hero Abhimanyu, destroyer of enemy heroes, killed it with one arrow.

verses.text:
तस्यावर्जितनागस्य कार्ष्णिः परपुरंजयः ।
राज्ञो रजतपुङ्खेन भल्लेनापहरच्छिरः ॥

meaning.en: When the elephant was down, Krishna's grandson, conqueror of enemy cities, took off the king's head with a silver-feathered broad-headed arrow.

verses.text:
विगाह्य तद्गजानीकं भीमसेनोऽपि पाण्डवः ।
व्यचरत्समरे मृद्नन्गजानिन्द्रो गिरीनिव ॥

meaning.en: Bhimasena the Pandava, plunging into that elephant army, moved through the battle crushing elephants, like Indra shattering mountains.

verses.text:
एकप्रहाराभिहतान्भीमसेनेन कुञ्जरान् ।
अपश्याम रणे तस्मिन्गिरीन्वज्रहतानिव ॥

meaning.en: In that battle we saw elephants killed by a single blow from Bhimasena, like mountains struck by the thunderbolt.

verses.text:
भग्नदन्तान्भग्नकटान्भग्नसक्थांश्च वारणान् ।
भग्नपृष्ठान्भग्नकुम्भान्निहतान्पर्वतोपमान् ॥

meaning.en: There were elephants with broken tusks, broken temples, broken thighs, broken backs and split foreheads, killed like mountains.

verses.text:
नदतः सीदतश्चान्यान्विमुखान्समरे गजान् ।
विमूत्रान्भग्नसंविग्नांस्तथा विशकृतोऽपरान् ॥

meaning.en: Other elephants, bellowing and collapsing or turned away in battle, broke and trembled, some voiding urine and dung.

verses.text:
भीमसेनस्य मार्गेषु गतासून्पर्वतोपमान् ।
अपश्याम हतान्नागान्निष्टनन्तस्तथापरे ॥

meaning.en: On Bhimasena's paths we saw dead elephants like mountains, and others groaning.

verses.text:
वमन्तो रुधिरं चान्ये भिन्नकुम्भा महागजाः ।
विह्वलन्तो गता भूमिं शैला इव धरातले ॥

meaning.en: Other great elephants, with split foreheads, vomiting blood and staggering, fell on the ground like mountains.

verses.text:
मेदोरुधिरदिग्धाङ्गो वसामज्जासमुक्षितः ।
व्यचरत्समरे भीमो दण्डपाणिरिवान्तकः ॥

meaning.en: With limbs smeared in fat and blood and drenched in marrow, Bhima moved in the battle like Death with his staff in hand.

verses.text:
गजानां रुधिराक्तां तां गदां बिभ्रद्वृकोदरः ।
घोरः प्रतिभयश्चासीत्पिनाकीव पिनाकधृक् ॥

meaning.en: Wielding that mace dripping with elephants' blood, Vrikodara was terrible and fearful, like the Pinaka-bearer holding Pinaka.

verses.text:
निर्मथ्यमानाः क्रुद्धेन भीमसेनेन दन्तिनः ।
सहसा प्राद्रवञ्शिष्टा मृद्नन्तस्तव वाहिनीम् ॥

meaning.en: Churned by the enraged Bhimasena, the remaining elephants suddenly fled, trampling your own army.

verses.text:
तं हि वीरं महेष्वासाः सौभद्रप्रमुखा रथाः ।
पर्यरक्षन्त युध्यन्तं वज्रायुधमिवामराः ॥

meaning.en: The great archers and chariot-warriors led by Subhadra's son guarded that hero as he fought, as the immortals guard the wielder of the thunderbolt.

verses.text:
शोणिताक्तां गदां बिभ्रदुक्षितो गजशोणितैः ।
कृतान्त इव रौद्रात्मा भीमसेनो व्यदृश्यत ॥

meaning.en: Holding his mace red with blood, drenched in the blood of elephants, the terrible Bhimasena looked like Death himself.

verses.text:
व्यायच्छमानं गदया दिक्षु सर्वासु भारत ।
नृत्यमानमपश्याम नृत्यन्तमिव शंकरम् ॥

meaning.en: We saw him, Bharata, whirling about with his mace in all directions, as though dancing, like Shankara dancing.

verses.text:
यमदण्डोपमां गुर्वीमिन्द्राशनिसमस्वनाम् ।
अपश्याम महाराज रौद्रां विशसनीं गदाम् ॥

meaning.en: We saw, great king, that dreadful, heavy, slaughtering mace, like the staff of Yama, sounding like Indra's thunderbolt.

verses.text:
विमिश्रां केशमज्जाभिः प्रदिग्धां रुधिरेण च ।
पिनाकमिव रुद्रस्य क्रुद्धस्याभिघ्नतः पशून् ॥

meaning.en: Mixed with hair and marrow and smeared with blood, it was like the Pinaka of enraged Rudra when he strikes beasts.

verses.text:
यथा पशूनां संघातं यष्ट्या पालः प्रकालयेत् ।
तथा भीमो गजानीकं गदया पर्यकालयत् ॥

meaning.en: As a herdsman drives a herd of cattle with his stick, so Bhima drove the elephant army with his mace.

verses.text:
गदया वध्यमानास्ते मार्गणैश्च समन्ततः ।
स्वान्यनीकानि मृद्नन्तः प्राद्रवन्कुञ्जरास्तव ॥

meaning.en: Struck on every side by the mace and by arrows, your elephants fled, trampling their own divisions.

verses.text:
महावात इवाभ्राणि विधमित्वा स वारणान् ।
अतिष्ठत्तुमुले भीमः श्मशान इव शूलभृत् ॥

meaning.en: Having scattered the elephants like a great wind scattering clouds, Bhima stood in the tumult like the trident-bearer in a cremation ground.
